p.EVERY-COMMIT-MESSAGE-FOLLOWS-CONVENTIONA: Every commit message follows the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) specification: a **typed header** and a body that explains *why*.

facts.HEADER-SUBJECT-LENGTH-MOOD-AND-CASE: Subject **≤ 60 characters** (hard limit 72), imperative mood, lowercase after the prefix.
facts.HEADER-SCOPE-IS-THE-NARROWEST-ACCURATE-S: `scope` names the **narrowest accurate** subsystem (a crate, package, module, or area).

p.BODY-A-BLANK-LINE-THEN-A-FREE-FORM-WHY: A blank line after the subject, then a free-form body that answers *why*, not *what* — the diff already shows what changed.

facts.NEVER-SUMMARISE-WHAT-CHANGED: Never write a subject that summarises *what* changed — write *why*.
facts.NEVER-CAPITALISE-OR-OMIT-THE-TYPE: Never capitalise the first word after the `type(scope):` prefix, and never omit the type.

p.FORMAT-DOES-NOT-ENFORCE-ATOMICITY: Conventional Commits is the message **format**; it does not by itself enforce **atomicity** (one commit = one logical idea).

p.A-VALID-MESSAGE-CAN-STILL-VIOLATE-THE-AT: A `feat: add foo, bar, and baz` message is valid Conventional Commits *and* a violation of the atomic rule.

p.ATOMICITY-IS-THE-SEPARATE-FLOW-AND-THE-T: Atomicity is the separate `git-atomic-commits` flow; the two run together.
